subject: Re: On‑prem observability signal lifecycle & export runbook
messages:
From: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@finbank.com>

Cc: security@finbank.com
Date: 2026-11-29T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Observability export for on‑prem Redwood deployment — initial questions

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this — we have an upcoming private deployment of Redwood (VPC + on‑prem forwarder) and security wants to validate the observability plan before we sign the SOW. High level constraints:

- Logs and metrics must be forwarded to our Splunk HEC endpoint inside our DMZ (no internet egress from the enclave).
- Trace data (OpenTelemetry) should be sampled at 1% by default, with a path to increase to 10% during incident windows.
- Retention: we need raw logs for 90 days (hot), index/aggregates 1 year.
- Evidence required for SOC2: TLS mutual auth for egress, token rotation process, and a runbook covering failure modes (forwarder restarts, disk pressure, backpressure to Redwood).

Specific asks:
1) Draft runbook or checklist we can sign off on.
2) Expected daily log volume (GB/day) from the forwarder for a medium‑sized Redwood cluster (4 GPUS, ~10k req/day).
3) Ports/protocols/IPs required for the forwarder to communicate with Splunk and for the control plane (if any).

Can you put together a concise runbook + a short meeting later this week?

Appreciate it — Aaron
Aaron Liu
Head of Platform Security, FinBank

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@finbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T08:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Observability export for on‑prem Redwood deployment — initial questions

Aaron — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front and a proposed next step below.

1) Runbook: we have a draft we can share (attached) that covers forwarder setup, TLS mTLS config, token rotation cadence, and failure escalation. It also includes a checklist for SIEM onboarding (HEC token exchange, cert pinning).

2) Volume: for the config you describe (4‑GPU, ~10k requests/day, standard tokenization + traces at 1%), expect ~12–20 GB/day of logs and ~0.8–1.5 GB/day of trace payloads and metrics. If you enable debug sampling or increase trace sample rate to 10% during incidents, plan for ~6–10x trace volume spike. We’ll include a sizing table in the runbook.

3) Networking: forwarder needs outbound TCP to your Splunk HEC over 443 (we support HEC over TLS) and mTLS to be negotiated from the forwarder side; control plane callbacks (optional) use outbound HTTPS to the private control endpoint over 443. We can operate in a fully air‑gapped model with a push proxy if required — that option is in the runbook.

Next step: I’ve attached the draft runbook and a network egress matrix image. Marissa (Obs PM) — can you review the failure modes and add the incident play for trace overload + backpressure? Kimberly — please confirm token rotation and KMS/HSM integration notes.

If that looks ok, I recommend a 45‑minute runbook walkthrough with FinBank Sec + Infra this Thursday at 10:30 PT. Would that work on your side?

— Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Stephanie — got the draft, thanks. Quick clarifications before the walkthrough:

- The volumes you quoted look fine. Can you add an example retention storage estimate for 90 days hot + 1 year warm assuming 20 GB/day? We need that for procurement sizing.
- For mTLS we need certs from our internal PKI (no public CA). Can your forwarder accept client certs signed by our CA and rotate them every 90 days?
- Splunk HEC URL will be inside our DMZ (https://splunk-hec.finbank.internal:8088). Will your forwarder handle nonstandard port 8088?

Also: we require a signed runbook section that describes the default behavior when the forwarder cannot reach Splunk (disk buffering thresholds, alerting, and automatic throttling). Can Marissa include those thresholds?

Thursday 10:30 PT works for the core team. Please send the calendar invite and a Go‑To‑Meeting link.

Hi Aaron — I added the requested content to the runbook and a short annex with explicit thresholds. Highlights: 

- Retention storage calc (assumes gzip compressed event payloads): 20 GB/day * 90 days = ~1.8 TB hot; 20 GB/day * 365 = ~7.3 TB warm (we include a 1.2x safety factor). I’ll paste the table in the runbook and include CSV export for procurement.
- mTLS: our forwarder accepts client certs signed by customer PKI. We support cert rotation via an API call or via mounted secrets (KMS/HSM integration). Rotation every 90 days is supported; we recommend automation using your internal cert rotation job.
- Nonstandard ports: yes — the forwarder supports HEC on any TCP port; we only require outbound TCP/443 or outbound TCP/<custom_port> based on your DMZ rules.

Failure modes and thresholds (runbook excerpt):
- Buffering: local disk buffer configured at default 50 GB. At 75% (37.5 GB) the forwarder raises a WARN alert to the control plane and to a customer webhook.
- At 90% (45 GB) the forwarder enters prioritized export mode (drops non‑essential debug logs, keeps security/ingest traces).
- At 98% the forwarder halts new log writes and sends a critical alert to both Redwood oncall and the customer webhook.
- Backpressure behavior: forwarder will exponentially backoff export attempts starting at 2s, doubling to a 5m cap; admins can configure shorter caps.

I’ve attached the updated runbook PDF and a network egress matrix (PNG). I’ll also create the calendar invite for Thu 2026‑12‑09 10:30 PT and include a GTM link + breakout dial‑ins for your Sec/Infra teams.

If you’d like, we can also include a short on‑prem demo of the forwarder in a staging VM during the walkthrough.

Thanks — Marissa Cole
